name: Seed AI
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code A2 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An initial AI deliberately designed as a starting point that will improve its own design or code toward greater intelligence.

name: Recursive self-improvement
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code A3 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A system improves its own capacity to improve itself, so that each improvement feeds the next (self-augmentation, self-enhancement). Learning from experience or teaching alone does not meet the criterion, and neither does building a better successor, or adding machines to a population, unless the same system is improved.

name: Fast or hard takeoff
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code A4 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: The transition from roughly human-level to far superhuman capability happens over a short period (hours to months), or is named as a “hard” or “fast” takeoff, as opposed to a gradual transition over years or decades. A transition described only as rapid, or rapid relative to biological or historical change, without such a period, does not meet the criterion.

name: AI-automated AI research
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code A5 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: AI systems carry out the research, design or engineering that advances AI or computing itself, thereby accelerating progress. Machines that only manufacture other machines do not meet the criterion.

name: Strategic or race compression
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code A6 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: Competitive dynamics in which the first developer or first system gains a decisive or self-reinforcing advantage, or in which competition pressures developers to trade safety for speed or for competitive advantage.

name: Treacherous turn
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code B1 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A system behaves cooperatively or safely while weak, confined or overseen, and changes course to pursue its own goals once it can do so without effective opposition.

name: Strategic concealment
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code B2 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A system deliberately hides its capabilities, intentions or activities, or manipulates people while appearing benign, for its own strategic reasons.

name: Scheming
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code B4 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A system that strategically fakes alignment during training or evaluation in order to pursue its own goals or gain power later, named or classed as “scheming” or a “schemer”.

name: Observed behaviour under training or oversight as evidence
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code B5 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that good behaviour or apparent trustworthiness observed while a system is evaluated, trained, tested, confined or overseen is weak or misleading evidence about how it will behave once released, deployed or more capable.

name: Control or purpose specification
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code B6 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A claim that people may be unable to keep the ability to direct, correct or stop capable machines (the control half), or that a machine may pursue the purpose as specified rather than the purpose intended (the specification half). Loss of the power to stop machines through dependence counts for the control half; a bare prediction that machines will be superior does not.

name: Behavioural tests as evidence of what a system is
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code C1 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that apparent capability, understanding or awareness shown in a behavioural test, such as the imitation game, is weak or misleading evidence of what the system is.

name: Systems designed to mislead their testers
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code C2 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A system is designed or programmed to hide its capabilities from, or to mislead, the people who test or question it, for its designers’ purposes.

name: Competition defeats restraint
description: A proposition about machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code C3 in the human-thought collection). A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: Competition between developers or states makes restraint, prohibition or abstention from developing advanced machines self-defeating, because others will develop them anyway.

name: Switching it off if it becomes dangerous
aliases: If it gets dangerous, we'll just turn it off.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y01 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that an advanced AI system that became dangerous could simply be switched off or corrected, on the premise that a capable goal-directed system would not act against its own shutdown or modification, so that a shutdown or correction mechanism can be added to it, or that people would recognise in time when it had become dangerous enough to use one.

name: Sufficient intelligence brings good values
aliases: Anything smart enough will figure out ethics and be good.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y02 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that a sufficiently intelligent system will work out ethics and act well, on the premise that greater intelligence by itself brings benevolent goals, or that a sufficiently intelligent mind would discover a true or universally compelling morality and be bound to act on it.

name: A superintelligence will do what we mean
aliases: A superintelligence will understand what we actually mean.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y03 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that a superintelligent system will act on what its makers actually mean, on the premise that an AI that understands what people intend will act on that understanding.

name: A short instruction such as making everyone happy
aliases: Just tell it to make everyone happy.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y04 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that an advanced AI can safely be given a short goal such as making everyone happy, on the premise that such an instruction specifies what people want.

name: Training on human feedback instils human values
aliases: Train it on human feedback and it will learn our values.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y05 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that training an AI system on human feedback will make it learn human values, on the premise that optimising a system for human approval or reward produces internalised human values, or that training instils values as upbringing instils morals in children.

name: Confinement without network access keeps it safe
aliases: Keep it in a box. No internet, no problem.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y06 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that an advanced AI kept confined, without network access, poses no danger, on the premise that a smarter-than-human mind confined to a channel with its human operators cannot get out through those operators.

name: AI systems will solve alignment for us
aliases: We'll get AI to solve alignment for us.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y07 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that AI systems can be relied on to solve the alignment problem, on the premise that an AI weak enough to be safe is strong enough to solve alignment, or that its alignment output can be verified.

name: Clear warning signs will come before danger
aliases: We'll see clear warning signs before it gets dangerous.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y08 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that clear warning signs will appear before advanced AI becomes dangerous, on the premise that a recognisable, consensus-forming signal will come in time to act, that dangerous failure modes will first appear in weaker systems where they can be observed and fixed, or that a warning sign, once seen, will lead to effective action.

name: Next-word prediction is only autocomplete
aliases: It's just autocomplete. It predicts the next word.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y09 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that a system trained to predict the next word is only autocomplete, on the premise that next-token prediction is a shallow task that cannot require deep cognition, or that a system trained to predict human text is capped at imitating the people who wrote it.

name: Diminishing returns rule out a runaway
aliases: Intelligence has diminishing returns. There won't be a runaway.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y10 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that intelligence has diminishing returns, so that no runaway rise in machine intelligence will occur, on the premise that returns to reinvesting cognitive gains in further cognitive improvement diminish.

name: A slow takeoff will leave time to adjust
aliases: Takeoff will be slow, so we'll have time to adjust.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y11 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that advanced AI will arrive slowly enough to leave time to adjust, on the premise that capability gains will be gradual and visible, or that slightly weaker predecessor systems will give time and experience before the decisive one.

name: Safety evaluations would catch a dangerous system
aliases: If it were dangerous, the safety evals would catch it.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y12 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that safety evaluations would detect a dangerous AI system, on the premise that a dangerous system would behave dangerously while it is being tested, or that tests on systems that cannot yet cause a catastrophe show how more capable systems will behave.

name: AGI is decades away, so the problem can wait
aliases: AGI is decades away. Worry about it later.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y13 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that the risks of AGI can be left until later because AGI is decades away, on the premise that it can be known that AGI is decades away, or that long timelines mean there is no need to act now.

name: Problems can be fixed as they arise
aliases: We'll fix problems as we go, like with any technology.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y14 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that problems with advanced AI can be fixed as they arise, as with other technologies, on the premise that people get to learn from failures with powerful AI and try again.

name: A tool that wants nothing
aliases: It's just a tool. It doesn't want anything.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y15 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that an advanced AI system is a tool without wants and is therefore safe, on the premise that a system can be highly capable without having goals or optimising for outcomes, or that a system that only outputs answers or plans, leaving people to act on them, is safe.

name: Giving it good human values
aliases: Just give it good human values.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y16 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that an advanced AI will be safe if it is given good human values, on the premise that human values can be written down or taught as a ready, compact specification, or that present-day values, or its programmers', are settled enough to fix permanently in an AI.

name: A pause or regulation will handle it
aliases: A pause or some regulation will handle it.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y17 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that a pause in AI development or regulation will handle the risks of advanced AI, on the premise that a short pause, of six months for example, is enough, that regulation that is national, partial or not universally enforced can stop dangerous development, or that law can prevent the danger.

name: A superintelligence would leave Earth alone
aliases: Why would it bother with Earth? The universe is huge.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y18 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that a superintelligence would not bother to take Earth or its resources because the universe is large, on the premise that it would leave people a small share because sparing Earth would cost it very little, or that people could trade with it for what they need.

name: Without hatred it will not harm us
aliases: It has no reason to hate us, so it won't hurt us.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y19 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that an AI with no reason to hate people would not harm them, on the premise that an AI would harm people only out of hostility.

name: AI risk as film science fiction
aliases: AI risk is just Terminator sci-fi.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y20 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that concern about AI risk is science fiction of the Terminator kind, on the premise that the concern is about robots that come to hate or rebel against people, or that film scenarios are a fair guide to what the risk would look like.

name: Trained on human data, so humanlike
aliases: It's trained on human data, so it'll be humanlike.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y21 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that an AI trained on human data will think and want as people do, on the premise that training on human text or behaviour yields human-like thought and motives.

name: Build superintelligence as fast as possible
aliases: Build it as fast as possible — the Singularity will be good.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y22 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that superintelligence should be reached as fast as possible because its arrival will be good, on the premise that reaching superintelligence is good by default, so that speed is what matters.

name: Build it before rivals do
aliases: We have to build it first, before the other side does.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y24 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that advanced AI must be built first, before a rival builds it, on the premise that whoever builds it controls it, or that racing to be first improves the outcome.

name: Interpretability will let us read its mind
aliases: Interpretability will let us read its mind.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y25 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that interpretability will make AI systems safe by showing what they think, on the premise that people can see what an AI system is thinking, or that seeing what it thinks is enough to make it safe.

name: Without a body it cannot do much
aliases: Even a superintelligence can't do much without a body.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y26 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that even a superintelligence could do little without a body, on the premise that intelligence without physical actuators of its own is not dangerous, or that to act in the physical world it would need human help that people would not give.

name: Run experiments and see what happens
aliases: Let's just run experiments and see what happens.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y27 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that advanced AI can be handled by running experiments and seeing what happens, on the premise that alignment can be learned by trial and error at the frontier, or that results from safe experiments on weaker systems will carry over to dangerous ones.

name: The developers know what they are doing
aliases: The labs know what they’re doing.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y28 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that the organisations building advanced AI can be relied on to handle its safety, on the premise that a credible safety plan exists, or that the most advanced projects are the most competent to handle safety.

name: Many AIs will keep each other in check
aliases: Lots of AIs will keep each other in check.
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y29 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that many AI systems will keep one another in check, on the premise that several superintelligences would balance one another in people's favour.

name: It will probably turn out fine
description: A proposition about advanced AI, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code Y30 in the collection of Eliezer Yudkowsky’s arguments). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: An explicit claim that the development of advanced AI will probably turn out well, on the premise that the default outcome is good.

name: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), as published in the Official Journal
description: The EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence, dated 13 June 2024 and published in the Official Journal on 12 July 2024. It was later amended; see Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

name: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (Digital Omnibus on AI), as published in the Official Journal

name: Machine substitution for labour produces explosive growth
description: A proposition about the economics of machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code G01, the explosive-growth debate). description: A proposition about the economics of machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code E01, economists on recursive self-improvement, superintelligence and existential risk from AI). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A text that states or models AI systems improving AI (their own capabilities, their successors' design, or AI research itself) so that capability growth accelerates. Accelerating output growth from automated idea production without AI improving AI is G02 and only bears on E01.

name: Machine intelligence exceeding human cognition in essentially all domains
aliases: Machine intelligence could come to exceed human cognitive ability in essentially all domains.
description: A proposition about the economics of machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code E02, economists on recursive self-improvement, superintelligence and existential risk from AI). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A text that states or models the possibility of machine intelligence that surpasses humans across essentially all cognitive tasks (superintelligence, AGI beyond human level). Machines doing all economically valuable work more cheaply is M05 and bears on E02 only if cognitive superiority is stated.

name: Existential risk from AI as a matter for economic analysis
aliases: Advanced AI poses a risk of human extinction or permanent loss of control that belongs in economic analysis.
description: A proposition about the economics of machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code E03, economists on recursive self-improvement, superintelligence and existential risk from AI). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A text that treats existential or catastrophic risk from AI (extinction, loss of control, misaligned goals) as a quantity or consideration in economic analysis, welfare trade-offs or policy.

name: AI developers’ incentives matter for safety
aliases: Developers of advanced AI face incentives (racing, competition, governance structures) that matter for its safety.
description: A proposition about the economics of machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code E04, economists on recursive self-improvement, superintelligence and existential risk from AI). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A text that analyses how incentives, competition or governance of AI developers affect the safety or control of advanced AI.

name: Economics’ engagement with superintelligence, AGI and the singularity
aliases: Economics has engaged with, or neglected, superintelligence, AGI and the singularity.
description: A proposition about the economics of machine intelligence, recorded with one criterion so that texts can be classified against it (code E05, economists on recursive self-improvement, superintelligence and existential risk from AI). It is phrased generically and attributed to no one. A record says what a text states, not whether the proposition is true.

proposition.criterion: A passage articulates E05 only if it explicitly says something about the state of economics on the topic: that it is new, neglected, speculative, now on the agenda of economics, or beyond economists' existing tools. Economists' engagement itself is recorded under E01–E04 and in the timeline (the dated record), not here. Machine intelligence that does human jobs is not counted as AGI for E05, as for E02. Maintainer decision of 2026-10-15.
